findings.claim: Only the formatter templates (object, string-key, enum, union) get the attribute. The resolver output is left undecorated: the user's `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]` partial class body, its nested FormatterCache/GetFormatter helper types, and any other generated files. The acceptance criterion says all generated code must be decorated, so the resolver's GetFormatter/cache code still counts toward coverage.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ExcludeFromCodeCoverageReceiptTests.EveryGeneratedSourceMentionsExcludeFromCodeCoverage. It runs the generator on a source with a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] and asserts every generated source text contains ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. The resolver file (Test.MyResolver.g.cs) should fail.

findings.claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so consumers building for netstandard2.0 or any .NET Framework target get no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage on any formatter. System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and in .NET Standard 2.0, so the guard is unnecessary. It leaves the requirement ('all generated code is decorated') unmet on exactly the targets many library authors multi-target.
